title: 18th BRICS Summit Opens in New Delhi as Leaders Adopt New Delhi Declaration
detail: The 18th BRICS Summit opened at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi under India's 2026 chairship, bringing together leaders of the 10-member bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, UAE) plus invited partner Saudi Arabia. Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Narendra Modi met on the sidelines amid US tariff pressure and the Iran war. Leaders unanimously adopted the 140-point New Delhi Declaration, which backs China and Russia's permanent UN Security Council seats and supports expanded UN roles for Brazil and India, pushes IMF/World Bank quota reform toward emerging economies, condemns the 2025 Pahalgam attack (26 killed) 'in the strongest terms' with 'zero tolerance' and 'no double standards' on terrorism, opposes unilateral sanctions and carbon border adjustment mechanisms, and calls for restoring WTO dispute settlement. The declaration makes no direct mention of Ukraine, reflecting the limits of consensus among members split on Russia's war.

title: BRICS Unveils De-Dollarization Payment Push as Trump Threatens 100% Tariffs
detail: At the New Delhi summit, leaders adopted BRICS Pay, a payment messaging network designed to give interoperability between India's UPI, China's CIPS and Russia's SPFS rails so members can settle cross-border trade in local currencies without dollar conversion. The New Delhi Declaration explicitly rules out a shared BRICS currency, framing the push as 'derisking' rather than full de-dollarization, and states there is 'no one-size-fits-all approach.' President Trump responded by threatening 100% tariffs on BRICS members, reiterating a warning first made over the bloc's earlier de-dollarization talk, even though BRICS Pay is a payment-messaging layer and not a reserve-currency replacement.
